## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `addpipe32` (32-bit registered adder: y = a + b (mod 2^32)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module addpipe32 (
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        valid_i,
    input  wire [31:0] a_i,
    input  wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg         valid_o,
    output reg  [31:0] y_o
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o     <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;

        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= a_i + b_i;
    end
end

endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607.

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: I'll start by replacing the generic `+` with an explicit Kogge-Stone prefix adder, which gives ABC a log-depth structure to map (timing dominates the score at 10 pts/ns vs 0.001 pts/um²).

Interesting — the explicit Kogge-Stone gave essentially the same area *and* WNS as the baseline, which suggests ABC already builds a log-depth adder, and a large chunk of the 2.5 ns path is fixed overhead (input delay, clock, setup) plus the tail logic after the adder.

Let me attack the logic *after* the adder: in the original, the D path is `sum → mux(valid) → and(rst_n) → D` (sync reset). I can move the reset out of the late data path.

Both variants land at WNS ≈ 7.45–7.49 with ~750 µm², so the path is ~8 gate levels of a near-minimal-depth adder plus a fixed overhead. Since the resizer doesn't upsize (slack is hugely positive), the only real lever is *removing a logic level*.

Trick: fold the final sum-XOR and the valid/reset mux into a single MUX2 selected by the carry (carry-select style), so the late carry sees exactly one cell before the flop — 7 levels instead of 8.

Three structural variants all landed slightly *below* the baseline (7.452 / 7.464 / 7.404 ns vs 7.487 ns), and all were larger in area. The pattern is clear: ABC's own delay-driven mapping of `a_i + b_i` plus the natural mux/reset tail is already at a local optimum (≈8 cell levels), the resizer never touches it (slack is hugely positive), and my hand-built prefix structures only add cells/wire load. Since area is worth only 0.001 pt/µm² (≈0.3 pt total upside) while each perturbation moves WNS by ±0.4 pt of noise, the highest expected-value use of my last submission is to lock in the known-best structure.
